subject: math
title: Grade 8 Central Tendency: Mean, Median, Mode and Range
seo_title: Grade 8 Mean, Median and Mode Worksheets: Range, Outliers and the Best Measure (Free, with Answer Key, BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on central tendency for the BC curriculum: find the mean, the median of odd and even counts, the mode and the range, with negative numbers, decimals and dot plots, and choose the best measure when data have an outlier. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Mean = sum ÷ count. Median = the middle value once the data are in order. Mode = the most common value.
key_sub: With an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values. The range (greatest − least) shows spread. An outlier pulls the mean toward it, so the median is often the better typical value.
body_html:
Three ways to describe a typical value

A measure of central tendency is one number that describes the centre of a data set: the mean, the median or the mode. The range is different: it tells how spread out the data are.

Seven quiz scores: 8, 5, 9, 6, 9, 3, 9. In order: 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9, 9.

MeasureHow to find itExample
MeanAdd all the values. Divide by how many values there are.49 ÷ 7 = 7
MedianPut the values in order. Take the middle one.3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9, 9 → 8
ModeThe value that appears most often9 appears 3 times → 9
RangeGreatest − least9 − 3 = 6

Median of an even number of values

With an even count there are two middle values. The median is their mean, so it can end in .5.

Example

Find the median of 12, 7, 10, 15, 9, 14.

In order: 7, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15. There are 6 values, so the middle values are the 3rd and 4th: 10 and 12. (10 + 12) ÷ 2 = 11.

Answer: 11

Data with negative numbers

Example

The low temperatures in Prince George on 5 days were −6, 2, −9, −1, 4 °C. Find the mean and the range.

Mean: −6 + 2 + (−9) + (−1) + 4 = −10, and −10 ÷ 5 = −2. Range: 4 − (−9) = 4 + 9 = 13.

Answer: mean −2°C, range 13°C

Read a dot plot

Each X is one value, and the X’s are already in order from left to right. Ten students told how many books they read last month.

Mean: 0 × 1 + 1 × 3 + 2 × 2 + 3 × 2 + 4 × 1 + 8 × 1 = 25, and 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5. Median: the 5th and 6th X’s from the left are both at 2, so the median is 2. Mode: the tallest stack is at 1. Range: 8 − 0 = 8.

Outliers and the best measure

An outlier is a value far from the others, like the 8 above. It pulls the mean toward it, but it barely moves the median. Here the mean (2.5) is greater than the median (2).

Use the …When …Example
Meanthe data have no outliers, or you want a fair share of a totalSharing a snack bill equally
Medianthe data have an outlierHouse prices, pay at a small business
Modeyou want the most common value, or the data are categoriesShoe sizes, favourite sport

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Taking the middle of the list without putting it in orderOrder the values from least to greatest first
Picking one middle value when the count is evenUse the mean of the two middle values
Ignoring the signs of negative numbers−9 is less than −1; add negatives as negatives
Giving the count as the mode (“3 times”)The mode is the value that repeats, not how many times
Giving the greatest value as the rangeRange = greatest − least
Using the mean when there is an outlierThe median describes a typical value better

faq.q: Is central tendency taught in Grade 8 in BC?
faq.a: Yes. Central tendency is a Grade 8 content standard in the Data and probability area of the BC math curriculum. Students find the mean, median and mode, and decide which one best describes a data set.

faq.q: How do you find the median when there is an even number of values?
faq.a: Put the values in order and find the two middle ones, then take their mean. For 7, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15 the middle values are 10 and 12, so the median is 11.

faq.q: When is the median better than the mean?
faq.a: When the data have an outlier. One very large or very small value pulls the mean toward it, but the median stays near the middle of the data.

faq.q: Is the range a measure of central tendency?
faq.a: No. The mean, median and mode describe a typical value. The range (greatest − least) describes how spread out the data are.

items.q: Harjot swam at the community pool on 6 days. The numbers of lengths he swam are 36, 29, 33, 31, 21, 12. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 36 + 29 + 33 + 31 + 21 + 12 = 162. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 162 ÷ 6 = 27.

items.q: Jasleen cycled every week for 7 weeks. The distances, in kilometres, are 27, 36, 33, 33, 34, 34, 27. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 27 + 36 + 33 + 33 + 34 + 34 + 27 = 224. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 224 ÷ 7 = 32.

items.q: In a survey, 7 students timed their SkyTrain ride to school. The times, in minutes, are 40, 22, 30, 36, 17, 32, 19. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 40 + 22 + 30 + 36 + 17 + 32 + 19 = 196. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 196 ÷ 7 = 28.

items.q: Mei read for 7 days. She read a mean of 21 pages per day. How many pages did she read in all?
items.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count = 21 × 7 = 147 pages.

items.q: Ethan’s scores on 7 math quizzes (out of 50) are 41, 37, 40, 32, 41, 47, 35. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 41 + 37 + 40 + 32 + 41 + 47 + 35 = 273. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 273 ÷ 7 = 39.

items.q: The numbers of students on 5 school buses in Kelowna are 48, 48, 32, 30, 48. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 48 + 48 + 32 + 30 + 48 = 206. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 206 ÷ 5 = 41.2.

items.q: Ji-woo read every day for 7 days. The numbers of pages she read are 38, 48, 15, 34, 46, 15, 35. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 38 + 48 + 15 + 34 + 46 + 15 + 35 = 231. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 231 ÷ 7 = 33.

items.q: Ava’s hockey team scored these numbers of goals in 5 games: 2, 1, 6, 1, 5. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 2 + 1 + 6 + 1 + 5 = 15. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

items.q: Hana’s times, in seconds, in 4 races of 100 m are 15.3, 13.1, 13.3, 15.9. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 15.3 + 13.1 + 13.3 + 15.9 = 57.6. There are 4 values, so divide by 4: 57.6 ÷ 4 = 14.4.

items.q: The low temperatures, in °C, in Prince George on 6 days in January were −2, −3, 1, −8, 2, −8. What is the mean temperature?
items.e: Add the values: −2 + (−3) + 1 + (−8) + 2 + (−8) = −18. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: −18 ÷ 6 = −3. Add the negative numbers as negatives: the signs matter.

items.q: A lacrosse team scored a mean of 11 goals per game in 8 games. How many goals did the team score in all?
items.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count = 11 × 8 = 88 goals.

items.q: Lucas scored these points in 5 basketball games: 16, 15, 13, 11, 12. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 16 + 15 + 13 + 11 + 12 = 67. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 67 ÷ 5 = 13.4.

items.q: The temperatures, in °C, at the top of Whistler Mountain at 8 a.m. on 6 days were −15, 0, 3, 3, 0, −9. What is the mean temperature?
items.e: Add the values: −15 + 0 + 3 + 3 + 0 + (−9) = −18. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: −18 ÷ 6 = −3. Add the negative numbers as negatives: the signs matter.

items.q: The lengths, in metres, of 5 long jumps by Chloe at a track meet in Kamloops are 4.2, 5.2, 5.2, 3.7, 4.2. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 4.2 + 5.2 + 5.2 + 3.7 + 4.2 = 22.5. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 22.5 ÷ 5 = 4.5.

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 30. Four of them are 33, 28, 28, 29. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 5 numbers must be 5 × 30 = 150. The known numbers add to 33 + 28 + 28 + 29 = 118. Missing number = 150 − 118 = 32.

items.q: The low temperatures, in °C, in Kamloops on 6 nights in December were 1, −15, −11, −15, 2, −4. What is the mean temperature?
items.e: Add the values: 1 + (−15) + (−11) + (−15) + 2 + (−4) = −42. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: −42 ÷ 6 = −7. Add the negative numbers as negatives: the signs matter.

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 26. Four of them are 19, 33, 23, 19. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 5 numbers must be 5 × 26 = 130. The known numbers add to 19 + 33 + 23 + 19 = 94. Missing number = 130 − 94 = 36.

items.q: The daily rainfall in Vancouver, in millimetres, for 5 days in November was 14, 17, 12, 14, 8. The mean is 13. Then the value 22 is added to the data. What is the new mean?
items.e: The new sum is 65 + 22 = 87, and now there are 6 values. New mean = 87 ÷ 6 = 14.5. (Do not just average the old mean and the new value.)

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 22. Four of them are 22, 23, 23, 15. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 5 numbers must be 5 × 22 = 110. The known numbers add to 22 + 23 + 23 + 15 = 83. Missing number = 110 − 83 = 27.

items.q: The new snowfall at Whistler, in centimetres, on 5 days in January was 7, 22, 7, 25, 14. The mean is 15. Then the value 6 is added to the data. What is the new mean?
items.e: The new sum is 75 + 6 = 81, and now there are 6 values. New mean = 81 ÷ 6 = 13.5. (Do not just average the old mean and the new value.)

sets.title: Find the median: odd and even counts

items.q: The lengths, in kilometres, of 5 hiking trails on Vancouver Island are 12, 5, 3, 14, 13. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 3, 5, 12, 13, 14. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: 12. (The middle of the list as written, 3, is not the median.)

items.q: Nadia’s hockey team scored these numbers of goals in 6 games: 4, 0, 0, 2, 5, 3. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 0, 0, 2, 3, 4, 5. With 6 values, there are two middle values, the 3rd and 4th: 2 and 3. The median is their mean: (2 + 3) ÷ 2 = 2.5.

items.q: The new snowfall at Whistler, in centimetres, on 9 days in January was 9, 5, 35, 12, 30, 2, 11, 7, 33. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 2, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 30, 33, 35. With 9 values, the middle one is the 5th: 11. (The middle of the list as written, 30, is not the median.)

items.q: Kai scored these points in 8 basketball games: 9, 22, 23, 6, 21, 25, 8, 17. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 6, 8, 9, 17, 21, 22, 23, 25. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 17 and 21. The median is their mean: (17 + 21) ÷ 2 = 19.

items.q: Zara read every day for 5 days. The numbers of pages she read are 22, 44, 25, 37, 30. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 22, 25, 30, 37, 44. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: 30. (The middle of the list as written, 25, is not the median.)

items.q: Noah’s scores on 10 math quizzes (out of 50) are 32, 30, 39, 42, 34, 42, 31, 29, 40, 45. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 29, 30, 31, 32, 34, 39, 40, 42, 42, 45. With 10 values, there are two middle values, the 5th and 6th: 34 and 39. The median is their mean: (34 + 39) ÷ 2 = 36.5.

items.q: The heights, in centimetres, of 6 cedar seedlings in a school garden are 38, 35, 23, 27, 19, 27. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 19, 23, 27, 27, 35, 38. With 6 values, there are two middle values, the 3rd and 4th: 27 and 27. Both are 27, so the median is 27.

items.q: In a survey, 5 students timed their SkyTrain ride to school. The times, in minutes, are 35, 34, 22, 24, 37. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 22, 24, 34, 35, 37. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: 34. (The middle of the list as written, 22, is not the median.)

items.q: Volunteers counted bald eagles near Squamish on 6 mornings. The counts are 84, 75, 23, 49, 82, 36. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 23, 36, 49, 75, 82, 84. With 6 values, there are two middle values, the 3rd and 4th: 49 and 75. The median is their mean: (49 + 75) ÷ 2 = 62.

items.q: Emma says the median of 15, 10, 29, 4, 17 is 29, because 29 is in the middle of the list. What mistake did she make?
c: She did not put the values in order first.
She should have found greatest − least.
She should have used the value that appears most often.
She should have added the values and divided by 5.
items.e: Put the values in order first: 4, 10, 15, 17, 29. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: 15. Emma took the middle of the list without putting the values in order. In fact, 29 is the greatest value.

items.q: The dot plot shows how many hours each member of a Victoria school band practised last week. What is the median?
items.e: There are 14 X’s, already in order from left to right. The two middle X’s are the 7th and 8th from the left. Both are above 5, so the median is 5.

items.q: The numbers of students on 5 school buses in Kelowna are 52, 36, 29, 28, 43. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 28, 29, 36, 43, 52. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: 36. (The middle of the list as written, 29, is not the median.)

items.q: Ryan swam at the community pool on 8 days. The numbers of lengths he swam are 34, 28, 35, 31, 16, 20, 18, 40. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 16, 18, 20, 28, 31, 34, 35, 40. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 28 and 31. The median is their mean: (28 + 31) ÷ 2 = 29.5.

items.q: The noon temperatures, in °C, in Fort St. John on 5 days in February were −1, −2, −19, −18, 3. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: −19, −18, −2, −1, 3. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: −2. Remember: −19 is less than −18, because it is farther below 0.

items.q: The lengths, in metres, of 5 long jumps by Ava at a track meet in Kamloops are 3.7, 4.7, 3.4, 3.5, 4.8. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 3.4, 3.5, 3.7, 4.7, 4.8. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: 3.7. (The middle of the list as written, 3.4, is not the median.)

items.q: A Grade 8 class in Surrey wrote a 10-point quiz. The dot plot shows the scores. What is the median?
items.e: There are 14 X’s, already in order from left to right. The two middle X’s are the 7th and 8th from the left. Both are above 6, so the median is 6.

items.q: The temperatures, in °C, at the top of Whistler Mountain at 8 a.m. on 7 days were −2, −3, 3, −15, −13, 2, −8. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: −15, −13, −8, −3, −2, 2, 3. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: −3. Remember: −15 is less than −13, because it is farther below 0.

items.q: The masses, in kilograms, of 7 coho salmon caught on a fishing trip on the Fraser River are 2.3, 4.1, 3.6, 4.7, 2.4, 4.3, 4.4. What is the median?
items.e: Put the values in order first: 2.3, 2.4, 3.6, 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.7. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 4.1. (The middle of the list as written, 4.7, is not the median.)

items.q: Students in a class in Prince George counted the letters in their first names. What is the median?
items.e: There are 13 X’s, already in order from left to right. The median is the 7th X from the left. It is above 5, so the median is 5.

items.q: A data set has 12 values, in order from least to greatest. How do you find the median?
c: Find the mean of the 1st and 12th values.
Find the mean of the 6th and 7th values.
items.e: With an even count there is no single middle value. The 6th and 7th values are in the middle (5 values before them and 5 after), so the median is their mean.

items.q: Simran read every day for 8 days. The numbers of pages she read are 37, 40, 22, 22, 29, 44, 44, 44. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 44 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 44, not the count 3.

items.q: The new snowfall at Whistler, in centimetres, on 9 days in January was 4, 9, 15, 15, 23, 9, 15, 6, 5. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 15 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 15, not the count 3.

items.q: The ages of 6 people on a whale-watching tour from Victoria are 55, 48, 61, 39, 44, 32. What is the mode?
items.e: Each value appears only once, so no value is more common than the others. The data set has no mode. (The mode is never a count like 1, and it is not 0.)

items.q: The heights, in centimetres, of 10 cedar seedlings in a school garden are 18, 26, 36, 32, 37, 32, 35, 34, 32, 37. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 32 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 32, not the count 3.

items.q: Owen’s scores on 9 math quizzes (out of 50) are 36, 31, 48, 47, 36, 31, 49, 28, 40. What is the mode?
items.e: 31 and 36 each appear 2 times. Every other value appears once. A data set can have two modes: 31 and 36.

items.q: In a survey, 9 students timed their SkyTrain ride to school. The times, in minutes, are 14, 22, 13, 41, 37, 41, 13, 38, 13. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 13 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 13, not the count 3.

items.q: The dot plot shows the goals Nadia’s hockey team scored in each game this season. What is the mode?
items.e: The tallest stack of X’s is above 3, so the mode is 3. (The stack has 4 X’s, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: Students in a Grade 8 class in Kelowna named their favourite sport: soccer 6, volleyball 4, lacrosse 10 and basketball 7. What is the mode?
items.e: The mode is the answer chosen most often. Lacrosse was chosen 10 times, more than any other sport, so the mode is lacrosse. The mode is the category, not the number 10.

items.q: Olivia scored these points in 6 basketball games: 23, 24, 16, 25, 28, 17. What is the mode?
items.e: Each value appears only once, so no value is more common than the others. The data set has no mode. (The mode is never a count like 1, and it is not 0.)

items.q: The low temperatures, in °C, in Prince George on 9 days in January were −5, −1, −23, −14, −14, −22, −2, −2, −2. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: −2 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value −2, not the count 3.

items.q: A shoe store in Burnaby sold these sizes of running shoes on Saturday: 9, 6.5, 7, 6.5, 10, 9.5, 6, 8, 8, 6.5. What is the mode?
items.e: 6.5 appears 3 times, more than any other size, so the mode is 6.5. Half sizes count as their own values.

items.q: Zara swam at the community pool on 8 days. The numbers of lengths she swam are 39, 18, 36, 36, 30, 31, 17, 39. What is the mode?
items.e: 36 and 39 each appear 2 times. Every other value appears once. A data set can have two modes: 36 and 39.

items.q: Students in a class in Nanaimo counted the pets they have at home. What is the mode?
items.e: The tallest stack of X’s is above 1, so the mode is 1. (The stack has 4 X’s, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: Arjun cycled every week for 8 weeks. The distances, in kilometres, are 32, 32, 40, 12, 37, 40, 19, 40. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 40 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 40, not the count 3.

items.q: Which measure is always one of the values in the data set (when it exists)?
items.e: The mode is a value that appears in the data most often, so it is always a data value. The mean and the median of an even count are often not in the data: the median of 2, 4, 9, 10 is 6.5.

items.q: The temperatures, in °C, at the top of Whistler Mountain at 8 a.m. on 9 days were −14, −8, −3, −3, −3, −5, 2, −6, −5. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: −3 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value −3, not the count 3.

items.q: A class in Victoria recorded each student’s favourite colour. Which measure can describe this data?
items.e: Colours are categories, not numbers. You cannot add them (no mean) or put them in number order (no median). You can still find the colour chosen most often, so the mode works.

items.q: A soccer team in Surrey ordered cleats in these sizes: 7.5, 10, 10, 6.5, 6, 9.5, 10, 9.5, 7.5. What is the mode?
items.e: 10 appears 3 times, more than any other size, so the mode is 10. Half sizes count as their own values.

items.q: A Grade 8 class in Surrey wrote a 10-point quiz. The dot plot shows the scores. What is the mode?
items.e: The tallest stack of X’s is above 5, so the mode is 5. (The stack has 4 X’s, but the mode is the value, not the count.)

items.q: The data are 5, 10, 10, 12, 18. Which value could you add so that the data set has two modes?
items.e: Right now 10 appears twice and is the only mode. Adding 12 makes 12 appear twice too, so 10 and 12 are both modes. Adding 10 gives 10 three times (one mode). A new value like 6 or 14 appears only once.

items.q: The new snowfall at Whistler, in centimetres, on 7 days in January was 5, 4, 12, 13, 22, 28, 16. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 28 − 4 = 24. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: Volunteers counted bald eagles near Squamish on 6 mornings. The counts are 66, 41, 81, 28, 80, 62. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 81 − 28 = 53. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: Which statement about the range of a data set is true?
c: It shows how spread out the data are.
It is the most common value.
items.e: The range is greatest − least. It tells how spread out the data are. It is not a measure of central tendency, because it does not give a typical value.

items.q: Ethan’s scores on 6 math quizzes (out of 50) are 35, 50, 43, 33, 32, 49. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 50 − 32 = 18. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: A Grade 8 class in Surrey wrote a 10-point quiz. The dot plot shows the scores. What is the range?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 4 and the X farthest to the right is at 9. Range = 9 − 4 = 5. Use the X’s, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: In a survey, 7 students timed their SkyTrain ride to school. The times, in minutes, are 15, 31, 39, 33, 12, 19, 14. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 39 − 12 = 27. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: The temperatures, in °C, at the top of Whistler Mountain at 8 a.m. on 6 days were −6, 2, −13, 3, 2, −11. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 3 − (−13) = 3 + 13 = 16. Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its opposite.

items.q: The lengths, in metres, of 8 long jumps by Hana at a track meet in Kamloops are 4.2, 3.4, 5.2, 4.4, 4.1, 5.2, 4.7, 4.3. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 5.2 − 3.4 = 1.8. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: Wei cycled every week for 6 weeks. The distances, in kilometres, are 30, 12, 38, 33, 17, 25. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 38 − 12 = 26. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: Students in a Grade 8 class in Kamloops counted the books they read over the summer. What is the range?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 2 and the X farthest to the right is at 8. Range = 8 − 2 = 6. Use the X’s, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: The range of Lucas’s bowling scores in 5-pin bowling is 70. His lowest score is 130. What is his highest score?
items.e: Range = highest − lowest, so highest = lowest + range = 130 + 70 = 200.

items.q: The low temperatures, in °C, in Prince George on 8 days in January were −12, −24, 1, −19, 2, −4, −4, 1. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 2 − (−24) = 2 + 24 = 26. Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its opposite.

items.q: The data are 5, 22, 24, 28. Which value could you add without changing the range?
items.e: The range is 28 − 5 = 23. A new value between 5 and 28 does not change the greatest or least value, so 6 keeps the range at 23. The other values are outside, so they make the range larger.

items.q: The masses, in kilograms, of 6 coho salmon caught on a fishing trip on the Fraser River are 4.1, 4.2, 3.5, 2.4, 2.6, 3.7. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 4.2 − 2.4 = 1.8. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: Over one week in Fort St. John, the highest temperature was 0°C and the range of the temperatures was 18°C. What was the lowest temperature?
items.e: Range = highest − lowest, so lowest = highest − range = 0 − 18 = −18°C.

items.q: Students in a class in Burnaby recorded how many hours they slept last night. What is the range?
items.e: The X farthest to the left is at 7 and the X farthest to the right is at 10. Range = 10 − 7 = 3. Use the X’s, not the ends of the number line.

items.q: The low temperatures, in °C, in Kamloops on 6 nights in December were −3, −12, −8, −8, 1, −7. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 1 − (−12) = 1 + 12 = 13. Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its opposite.

items.q: Owen recorded minutes of homework on 6 school nights: 46, 27, 44, 28, 22, 33. Sofia recorded 37, 48, 33, 27, 36, 30. How much greater is the range of Owen’s data than the range of Sofia’s data?
The numbers of students on 4 school buses in Kelowna are 34, 24, 49, 31. One more value is added. It is greater than all the others, and the new range is 36. What is the new value?
items.e: The least value is still 24. New range = new value − least, so new value = 24 + 36 = 60.

items.q: Olivia recorded kilometres cycled in 6 weeks: 19, 25, 5, 16, 6, 18. Kai recorded 13, 26, 28, 12, 17, 19. How much greater is the range of Olivia’s data than the range of Kai’s data?

sets.title: Word problems: outliers and the best measure

items.q: The high temperatures, in °C, in Kelowna on 7 days in July were 35, 34, 32, 33, 33, 13, 31. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 31 and 35. The value 13 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: Five friends spent $12, $9, $17, $4, $13 on snacks for a BC Ferries trip. They want everyone to pay the same amount. How much should each person pay in the end?
items.e: Sharing the total equally is the mean: 12 + 9 + 17 + 4 + 13 = 55, and 55 ÷ 5 = $11. The mean is the fair-share value.

items.q: The ages of 8 people on a hike up Grouse Mountain are 41, 11, 35, 33, 31, 39, 38, 41. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 31 and 41. The value 11 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: Arjun rode his bike every day for 7 days. The distances, in kilometres, were 11, 9, 12, 11, 15, 61, 14. The outlier, 61, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 61 there are 6 values. Their sum is 11 + 9 + 12 + 11 + 15 + 14 = 72. Mean = 72 ÷ 6 = 12. (With the outlier, the mean was 133 ÷ 7 = 19.)

items.q: The numbers of visitors to a small museum in Nanaimo on 7 weekdays were 54, 41, 63, 164, 59, 57, 45. Which measure best describes a typical value?
items.e: The outlier 164 pulls the mean up to 69, which is greater than every other value. The median, 57, stays in the middle of the data, so the median describes a typical value better.

items.q: A shoe store in Victoria is ordering new hiking boots. It wants to order the most pairs in the size that sells most often. Which measure should it use?
items.e: The size that sells most often is the mode. A mean size like 8.3 may not even exist, and the median does not tell which size is most popular.

items.q: Jasleen timed her bus ride to school in Surrey on 7 days. The times, in minutes, were 13, 18, 12, 41, 17, 16, 13. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 12 and 18. The value 41 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: The numbers of pages in 7 novels in a classroom library are 243, 257, 244, 198, 673, 192, 258. The outlier, 673, is removed. By how much does the mean decrease?
items.e: With the outlier: 2065 ÷ 7 = 295. Without it: 1392 ÷ 6 = 232. The mean decreases by 295 − 232 = 63.

items.q: The prices, in dollars, of 6 used snowboards for sale in Kelowna are 147, 180, 167, 120, 146, 479. The outlier, 479, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 479 there are 5 values. Their sum is 147 + 180 + 167 + 120 + 146 = 760. Mean = 760 ÷ 5 = 152. (With the outlier, the mean was 1239 ÷ 6 = 206.5.)

items.q: Ethan’s marks on the first 4 science tests are 72, 88, 89, 74 (out of 100). What mark does he need on the 5th test to have a mean of 80?
items.e: For a mean of 80 over 5 tests, the total must be 5 × 80 = 400. So far: 72 + 88 + 89 + 74 = 323. Ethan needs 400 − 323 = 77.

items.q: The numbers of salmon counted at a creek on Vancouver Island on 7 days are 31, 35, 34, 35, 24, 39, 33. On the 8th day, 105 salmon are counted. Which measure changes the most?
c: They all change by the same amount.
items.e: Before: mean 33, median 34, mode 35. After: mean 42, median 34.5, mode 35. The outlier 105 pulls the mean up by 9, but the median moves only 0.5 and the mode does not change.

items.q: The lengths, in centimetres, of 7 salmon caught on a fishing trip are 62, 62, 28, 65, 70, 63, 63. Which measure best describes a typical value?
items.e: The outlier 28 pulls the mean down to 59, which is less than every other value. The median, 63, stays in the middle of the data, so the median describes a typical value better.

items.q: Ji-woo recorded how many minutes she spent on homework on 8 school nights: 45, 26, 44, 34, 36, 7, 37, 42. The outlier, 7, is removed. By how much does the median change?
items.e: With the outlier: Put the values in order first: 7, 26, 34, 36, 37, 42, 44, 45. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 36 and 37. The median is their mean: (36 + 37) ÷ 2 = 36.5. Without it: Put the values in order first: 26, 34, 36, 37, 42, 44, 45. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 37. The median changes by only 37 − 36.5 = 0.5. An outlier hardly moves the median.

items.q: The masses, in kilograms, of 8 dogs at a dog park in Burnaby are 31, 32, 31, 18, 24, 32, 4, 25. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 18 and 32. The value 4 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: The heights, in centimetres, of 6 players on a Grade 8 volleyball team are 158, 194, 171, 163, 156, 172. The outlier, 194, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 194 there are 5 values. Their sum is 158 + 171 + 163 + 156 + 172 = 820. Mean = 820 ÷ 5 = 164. (With the outlier, the mean was 1014 ÷ 6 = 169.)

items.q: Wei bowled 175, 195, 140 in 3 games of 5-pin bowling. What score does he need in the 4th game to have a mean score of 180?
items.e: For a mean of 180 over 4 games, the total must be 4 × 180 = 720. So far: 175 + 195 + 140 = 510. Wei needs 720 − 510 = 210.

items.q: The numbers of cars waiting for a BC Ferries sailing at Horseshoe Bay on 7 weekday mornings were 107, 140, 133, 95, 134, 105, 336. The outlier, 336, is removed. By how much does the mean decrease?
items.e: With the outlier: 1050 ÷ 7 = 150. Without it: 714 ÷ 6 = 119. The mean decreases by 150 − 119 = 31.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °C, in Kelowna on 8 days in July were 32, 33, 36, 29, 29, 35, 31, 15. The outlier, 15, is removed. Which measure stays the same?
items.e: 29 still appears twice, so the mode stays 29. The mean changes from 30 to about 32, the median changes from 31.5 to 32, and the range gets much smaller.

items.q: The 7 people who work at a bike shop in Whistler earn these yearly pay amounts: $39 000, $40 000, $40 000, $41 000, $45 000, $47 000, $161 000. The highest amount is the owner’s. The owner says, “Pay here is high.” Which measure of central tendency makes the typical pay look highest?
items.e: Mean: $413 000 ÷ 7 = $59 000. Median (4th value): $41 000. Mode: $40 000. The owner’s large pay pulls the mean up, so it is the highest. The median, $41 000, describes a typical worker better.

items.q: Simran recorded her screen time, in minutes, for one week: 95, 55, 100, 30, 90, 55, 65. She wants the typical value to look as low as possible. Which measure of central tendency is lowest?
items.e: Mean: 490 ÷ 7 = 70. Median: Put the values in order first: 30, 55, 55, 65, 90, 95, 100. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 65. Mode: 55 appears twice, so it is 55. The mode is lowest here.
